title: Positive but variable effects of crop diversification on biodiversity and ecosystem services
methodology: Second-order meta-analysis of crop diversification effects.
limitations: High between-study variability; dryland water competition can reduce benefits if species are poorly chosen.

chunks.text: Crop diversification, including intercropping and agroforestry, shows positive average effects on biodiversity and several soil-related services, but the magnitude is highly variable. In water-limited systems, benefits depend on selecting drought-compatible species and avoiding excessive competition. The paper is evidence both for diversification and against transferring a single percentage gain to a new site.

Agroforestry and species mixtures often rank among the stronger diversification options for biodiversity, while cover crops show more mixed results depending on climate. This variability is scientifically important: conflicting local outcomes should be reported rather than averaged away when advising a specific farm.
